# REST API reference

Correlix publishes 205 documented operations across 20 groups. The table below is generated from the route table the server itself serves, so it cannot drift from the running API.

Fetch the machine-readable document from your own deployment:

```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  http://localhost:8000/api/openapi.json
```

## Authentication

Every operation takes one of two credentials in the `Authorization` header:

| Credential | Header | Obtained from |
|---|---|---|
| Access token (JWT) | `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` | `POST /api/auth/login` |
| API key | `Authorization: Bearer ntk_…` or `X-API-Key: ntk_…` | **Administration → API Access** |

A request without a credential is refused with `401` and the body `{"error":"missing bearer token"}`.

## Auth

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `DELETE` | `/api/auth/elevation` | End the caller's own elevated access immediately, before it expires on its own (self-scoped, audited) |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/elevation` | The elevated access the CALLER currently holds: which role, over what scope, why, and when it expires. Self-scoped — it answers about the caller and nobody else |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/locator` | Resolve a per-tenant sign-in URL (/t/&#123;slug&#125; or /org/&#123;org_id&#125;) to a candidate realm and arm the signed candidate cookie. Public; an unknown or inactive locator answers the same empty result as a known one, with no information leak |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/login` | Exchange username/password for an access + refresh token |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/logout` | Revoke a refresh token |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/me` | Current principal |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/permissions` | Effective module→level permission grid |
| `POST` | `/api/auth/refresh` | Rotate a refresh token for a fresh access token |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/sso/config` | SSO availability + provider buttons |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/sso/login` | Begin the OIDC Authorization Code flow |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/sso/tenant-idp` | This tenant's own identity-provider connections, with the sign-in and per-tenant callback URLs to hand an IdP team (administration:admin, own tenant only) |
| `DELETE` | `/api/auth/sso/tenant-idp/&#123;alias&#125;` | Delete one of this tenant's connections (administration:admin) |
| `GET` | `/api/auth/sso/tenant-idp/&#123;alias&#125;` | One of this tenant's connections. Another tenant's alias answers the same 404 as an unknown one (administration:admin) |
| `PUT` | `/api/auth/sso/tenant-idp/&#123;alias&#125;` | Create or edit a connection in the caller's OWN tenant. The owning tenant is stamped from the token and cannot be named in the body (administration:admin) |

## BGP

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/bgp/alerts` | The caller's BGP alert history plus the current incident class per watched prefix (visibility_loss \| origin_change \| rpki_invalid \| route_leak \| bogon \| none \| unknown) with the vantage points and paths that support it; answers enabled:false with an explanation unless FEATURE_BGP_ALERTS is on — an empty list is never rendered as 'all clear' |
| `DELETE` | `/api/bgp/alerts/baselines` | Forget one prefix's origin baseline (?prefix=, infrastructure:write). The next corroborated measurement becomes a new first observation, so whatever is announcing the prefix then becomes the baseline. 404 for a prefix the caller's tenant does not hold, which is the same answer another tenant's prefix gets |
| `GET` | `/api/bgp/alerts/baselines` | The origin baseline recorded per watched prefix: which AS was originating it the first time it was measured, how many collector peers corroborated that, and whether an operator has since accepted a different set. It is what a fully propagated origin change is detected against. A prefix absent from this list has no baseline, so an origin change on it would not be detected yet |
| `POST` | `/api/bgp/alerts/baselines` | Accept an origin set as the new baseline for one prefix (infrastructure:write; the owner is stamped from the token). This is how a legitimate re-homing stops alerting. The new origin is never taken from the current announcement automatically, and an open origin-change incident clears on the next MEASURED pass, not on the accept |
| `GET` | `/api/bgp/alerts/config` | The caller's declared alert policy: expected origin ASNs, upstream (transit) set and the visibility/corroboration thresholds, per prefix or as a tenant default |
| `PUT` | `/api/bgp/alerts/config` | Replace the caller's alert policy (infrastructure:write; the owner is stamped from the token, never the body). An empty expected-origin set falls back to the prefix's RECORDED origin baseline (/api/bgp/alerts/baselines), which is a remembered observation rather than a declared intent; a prefix with no baseline yet gets no origin check at all. An empty upstream set disables the route-leak heuristic rather than guessing a transit set |
| `GET` | `/api/bgp/aspa` | ASPA record for an ?resource=ASn — honest 'not configured' unless BGP_ASPA_PROVIDER_URL names a provider (no public per-ASN ASPA API exists) |
| `GET` | `/api/bgp/aspath-graph` | AS-path node-link graph for ?prefix= from RIS collector state (deduped, edges capped at 500) |
| `GET` | `/api/bgp/bogons` | Bogon prefixes seen on the caller's own BMP feed and update ring, with first/last seen and the peer, plus the set actually in force: the embedded IANA/RFC special-purpose blocks (source + transcription date included) and the OPTIONAL Team Cymru full-bogons feed when FEATURE_BGP_BOGON_FEED is on |
| `GET` | `/api/bgp/feed` | Near-live BGP updates for the caller's watchlist from a bounded per-tenant ring buffer (?since= cursor); requires FEATURE_BGP_LIVE_FEED |
| `GET` | `/api/bgp/geofeed` | RFC 8805 geofeed published for a prefix or ASN, discovered per RFC 9092 from the registry object |
| `GET` | `/api/bgp/resource` | Routing status, RPKI verdict, collector paths or registry ownership for one resource (?view=status\|updates\|whois) |
| `GET` | `/api/bgp/rpki` | RPKI origin validation for the caller's watchlist prefixes, or for one ?resource= prefix |
| `DELETE` | `/api/bgp/watchlist` | Stop watching a resource (?resource=) |
| `GET` | `/api/bgp/watchlist` | The caller's tenant watchlist of prefixes and ASNs |
| `POST` | `/api/bgp/watchlist` | Watch a prefix or ASN (tenant stamped from the token) |

## Data Protection

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/system/backup` | Data-protection intent + live DR status (platform admin) |
| `PUT` | `/api/system/backup` | Update the off-host destination, transport, full-backup schedule and bundle retention (retain_count: how many artifacts the host keeps, 0..365, 0 = pruning off; OMIT the field to leave the stored retention unchanged — it is never cleared by a partial write). The host applier writes it to BACKUP_KEEP (platform admin, audited) |
| `GET` | `/api/system/backup/coverage` | Per-engine backup coverage: OpenSearch snapshots, the Correlix system bundle, ClickHouse, Postgres, VictoriaMetrics, sealed secrets/TLS material and device config backups. Each engine reports covered yes\|no\|not_applicable\|unknown WITH a reason, schedule + whether the GUI governs it, last attempt and last SUCCESS, last restorability verification, size, retention, target (local\|remote\|offsite\|none) with immutable/encrypted flags, and the achieved RPO (age of the last good copy) judged against TWO separately-published numbers — rpo_target_hours, measured from the engine's own schedule, and rpo_objective_hours, the platform's DECLARED objective (24h per data store; 0 for the sealed custody material, whose envelope is change-driven rather than time-driven). Per-engine last_verified comes from the BUNDLE restore drill (scripts/backup-drill.sh), which restores a real artifact into disposable containers: a skipped or absent leg leaves the proof null with its reason, never green. Each store's row reflects its OWN component verdict inside the last bundle run (pass \| partial \| fail \| skip), so a night on which only one store's copy failed no longer reports the rest as failed — or that one as covered. Anything not measured is null plus a *_detail explaining why — never a zero |
| `GET` | `/api/system/backup/operations` | Recent snapshot operations (bounded ring, newest first) — kind, state, actor, target, progress, result, error |
| `GET` | `/api/system/backup/operations/&#123;id&#125;` | One operation's status; the poll target for every 202 above |
| `GET` | `/api/system/backup/snapshots` | The netops-daily Snapshot Management policy as the GUI renders it — enabled, schedule cron, retention (max_count / max_age_days), last run and next trigger — plus the repository's registration/verification state and, when the schedule is off, who turned it off and when |
| `PUT` | `/api/system/backup/snapshots` | Partial update of the snapshot schedule: enabled (rides the SM plugin's _start/_stop), schedule_cron (5 fields), retention_max_count (1..365), retention_max_age_days (0..3650, 0 = count-only). The stored GUI intent is authoritative — the opensearch-init bootstrap no longer re-enables a deliberately disabled policy (platform admin, audited) |
| `POST` | `/api/system/backup/snapshots/create` | Take one snapshot now. The name is generated server-side against a closed grammar — never client-supplied. Returns 202 + an Operation to poll (platform admin, audited) |
| `POST` | `/api/system/backup/snapshots/delete` | Delete one snapshot. Type-to-confirm: `confirm` must equal `snapshot` exactly, the same guard the tenant delete uses. Returns 202 + an Operation (platform admin, audited) |
| `GET` | `/api/system/backup/snapshots/list` | Inventory of the repository's snapshots, newest first: name, state, indices, shard totals/failures with reasons, started/ended, duration, size, and the restorability verdict (verified true\|false\|null with when and why) |
| `POST` | `/api/system/backup/snapshots/restore` | Restore a snapshot, or named indices from it. mode=renamed (default) restores under rename_prefix so nothing live is touched; mode=in_place overwrites the live indices and therefore REQUIRES the type-to-confirm token. Returns 202 + an Operation (platform admin, audited) |
| `POST` | `/api/system/backup/snapshots/verify` | Run the restorability probe on demand: restore the smallest index of the snapshot under a temporary name, compare doc counts against the source, delete the temporary index. Omit `snapshot` to probe the newest SUCCESS. Returns 202 + an Operation (platform admin, audited) |
| `GET` | `/api/system/storage/measured` | MEASURED bytes on disk, per store and per tenant where the store is tenant-partitioned at rest (tracker 204). Every number is read back from the store that owns the bytes by the query named in each reading's `source` — OpenSearch `_cat/indices` store.size (with `_nodes/stats/indices/store` as a platform-total-only fallback when the api's search account lacks indices:monitor/stats), ClickHouse `system.parts` bytes_on_disk grouped by table and partition (which carries the owning tenant, so the attribution is exact, and data_uncompressed_bytes beside it gives a MEASURED compression ratio), VictoriaMetrics' own vm_data_size_bytes, pg_database_size()/pg_total_relation_size(), and a walk of the api's own data directory. Kafka's log-directory size is NOT measurable from the api and says so. A store that could not be measured returns bytes_on_disk null plus a detail explaining why — never a zero, and never a figure derived from a rate times an assumed bytes-per-row; the derived sizing model lives in scripts/resource_planner.py and is labelled an estimate there. total_measured_bytes is a LOWER BOUND whenever unmeasured_stores is non-empty. Scoped: a tenant admin sees only its own tenant's bytes; a platform principal sees every tenant |

## Digital Experience

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/api/dem/business-events` | Ingest business outcomes (purchase, booking, claim, or whatever this tenant's business does — the type is a free string). Same credential, bounds and tenant-stamping as /api/dem/events. A value with no currency is refused: an unlabelled number is not an amount |
| `GET` | `/api/dem/changes` | The normalized change feed over the window (?window=, ?type=, ?app=, ?site=, ?limit=, ?offset=): deployments, config, feature flags, cloud, network, security policy, DNS and route changes on one timeline |
| `POST` | `/api/dem/changes` | Record a change event. Immutable: a repeated id is idempotent and never rewrites what was recorded. The owning tenant is stamped from the token |
| `GET` | `/api/dem/data-health` | Per-source experience telemetry health (?window=): configured, state, last seen, freshness, volume, coverage, whether the source can anchor a confirmed verdict, and how much its current state is lowering diagnostic confidence. UNKNOWN and NO DATA are never reported as healthy |
| `POST` | `/api/dem/events` | Ingest first-party experience events (RUM beacons, agent and API-client events). WRITE-ONLY, and gated by the dedicated tenant-bound `ingest:experience` API-key scope or an operator's infrastructure:write — the owning tenant is stamped from the credential and cannot be expressed in the body. user_ref must be a pseudonymous per-tenant reference; a direct identifier is REFUSED, never silently hashed. A full queue answers 503 with Retry-After rather than 202 for events with nowhere to go |
| `GET` | `/api/dem/experience` | The experience score over a 1h or 24h window: availability against the error budget, p95 latency against the declared budget and path stability, per target and rolled up per site and per app. A window with no measurement returns measured:false and a reason — never a fabricated zero |
| `GET` | `/api/dem/incidents` | Experience incidents derived from the window's evidence, worst first (?window=, ?severity=, ?app=, ?journey=, ?limit=, ?offset=). Each row carries the leading cause, its confidence and verdict tier, the owning seam and the impact dimensions that were NOT measured |
| `GET` | `/api/dem/incidents/&#123;id&#125;` | One experience incident: impact, ranked hypotheses with their confidence factors and gate reasons, supporting and contradicting evidence, missing evidence, correlation-ranked changes, ownership, recommended actions and the recovery-verification plan. An unknown or another tenant's id answers 404 |
| `GET` | `/api/dem/incidents/&#123;id&#125;/evidence` | The incident's evidence: every item with its stance, modality class, observer, reliability and provenance, plus the missing-evidence records that lower confidence and can block confirmation |
| `GET` | `/api/dem/incidents/&#123;id&#125;/path` | The immutable path-observation reference for the incident, to be rendered through the service path graph API (the single source of hop order). Returns measured:false with a reason when no forward path was observed — never a clean path nobody measured |
| `POST` | `/api/dem/incidents/&#123;id&#125;/promote` | Promote a DERIVED experience incident into the platform incident record (source_type experience), persisting the DEM evidence packet beside it. infrastructure:write; the owning tenant is stamped from the token. Idempotent — the derived id is the dedup key, so a second promotion folds into the same incident and escalates its severity rather than raising a twin. Answers 409 when the deployment has no incident system of record (it is Postgres-only), never a 202 for an incident nobody raised |
| `GET` | `/api/dem/incidents/&#123;id&#125;/timeline` | The incident's single timeline — impact, evidence and changes on one axis, each entry stating whether it was observed or inferred |
| `GET` | `/api/dem/journeys` | The tenant's declared user journeys with their measured health over the window (?window=): per-step success against the objective, the failing step, and the coverage behind the number |
| `POST` | `/api/dem/journeys` | Declare a journey (branching steps, optional steps, loops, business importance, SLO, step→target bindings). The owning tenant is stamped from the token — a tenant in the body cannot be expressed |
| `DELETE` | `/api/dem/journeys/&#123;id&#125;` | Remove a journey definition. The measurements its steps were bound to are unaffected |
| `GET` | `/api/dem/journeys/&#123;id&#125;` | One journey definition and its measured health. Another tenant's id answers 404 |
| `PUT` | `/api/dem/journeys/&#123;id&#125;` | Replace a journey definition; the version increments so an observation recorded against the old one is never silently re-attributed |
| `GET` | `/api/dem/overview` | The Experience overview over a 1h or 24h window (?window=): the published, decomposable experience score with its policy version, declared journeys and their measured health, open experience incidents, recent changes, hotspots and per-source telemetry confidence. A dimension nothing measured contributes nothing and is reported as not-measured with its reason; below the evidence minimum no score is published at all |
| `GET` | `/api/dem/synthetics/coverage` | The synthetic COVERAGE model (?window=): per declared user action, how many checks protect it, from how many vantages, when one last succeeded, and whether it is protected, thinly protected, untested, stale or broken. An action nothing measures is untested, never healthy |
| `GET` | `/api/dem/targets` | The caller's tenant's synthetic experience targets (icmp \| tcp \| dns \| http) with their site/app labels and latency/availability budgets; enabled:false plus an explanation when FEATURE_DEM is off |
| `POST` | `/api/dem/targets` | Declare an experience target. The owning tenant is stamped from the token — a tenant in the body is not merely ignored, it cannot be expressed |
| `DELETE` | `/api/dem/targets/&#123;id&#125;` | Remove an experience target. Its recorded series are unaffected and simply stop growing |
| `GET` | `/api/dem/targets/&#123;id&#125;` | One experience target. A target id owned by another tenant answers 404, never 403 — an id is never confirmed to exist |
| `PUT` | `/api/dem/targets/&#123;id&#125;` | Patch an experience target (edit, or pause it without deleting its history). The kind and the owning tenant are immutable |

## Incidents

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/incidents` | List the caller's own incidents, newest first, with optional status/severity/before filters and house paging. Tenant-scoped by the token's principal; a platform principal sees every tenant (alerts:read) |
| `POST` | `/api/incidents` | Open an investigation from an operator's own words: &#123;title, description?, severity?&#125; becomes a manual incident through the same seam an alert-born one uses. The owning tenant is stamped from the TOKEN — a tenant_id in the body is refused (400), and a platform-wide principal owns no tenant and is refused too. Idempotent by the store's dedup rule: describing the same symptom while the first is still open folds into it (200) rather than minting a second record (201) (alerts:write; audited) |

Carries an honest coverage block: vrf_labels says whether any interface series actually carried a vrf label, transport names the lane (snmp is INFERRED from an absent transport stamp), and every absent measurement is null with a note rather than zero (infrastructure:read; 404 outside the caller's tenant, identical to an absent device) |

## Licence

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `DELETE` | `/api/system/licence` | Remove the installed licence and return to the Community ceilings. Nothing is deleted from the platform itself; devices and data over a Community ceiling are listed as not covered, never removed (platform admin, audited) |
| `GET` | `/api/system/licence` | The licence in force, in ONE of two scopes decided by the caller, never by the request. scope=platform (the cross-tenant platform owner): customer, tier, ceilings with PLATFORM-WIDE usage and whether each is soft, the closed feature vocabulary with what is entitled, the expiry phase (valid \| in_grace \| post_grace) with days_to_expiry and grace_days_left, whether the licence is a trial, the over-ceiling items LISTED with when each overage began and the over-ceiling DEVICES named, the trusted public keys and the offline verification recipe. scope=tenant (any administration:admin caller, including a tenant/org admin, and the owner narrowed with as_tenant): tier, entitled features, the same ceilings with THIS TENANT'S OWN usage beside them, expiry state and managed_by — no customer, no licence id, no key material, no file path. No licence installed is a normal state and reports the Community ceilings, not an error |
| `PUT` | `/api/system/licence` | Install a licence document. The signature is verified BEFORE anything is written, so a refused upload never displaces a working licence and the exact reason is returned verbatim — an unknown signing key, a modified file and a malformed one are three different answers (platform admin, audited on both outcomes) |
| `GET` | `/api/system/licence/usage` | Recorded USAGE for a period — a separate data contract from the licence itself: entitlement says what a customer may do, this says what they actually consumed. Daily per-tenant rows (UTC day) with unique and peak monitored devices counted from CONFIGURATION rather than from telemetry activity, watched prefixes, tenant/org counts and the configured retention windows, plus diagnostic meters (metric samples and series, log and flow records accepted after processing, experience checks, hosted-AI tokens, pipeline in/out ratio). A meter with no counter on this installation is null with the reason beside it, never a zero. Scope is decided by the caller, never by the request: a tenant/org admin gets their own tenant, the platform owner gets every tenant plus the installation row and may narrow with ?tenant=; a scoped caller naming another tenant gets 404. from/to are UTC days and default to the last 30. Nothing is ever sent anywhere: there is no phone-home |
| `GET` | `/api/system/licence/usage/report` | The same period as a SIGNED JSON document, for download. Carries the daily rows as well as the totals so the arithmetic can be redone independently, the meter definitions so it explains its own columns, and an ed25519 signature over canonical bytes (sorted keys, no whitespace, UTF-8) made by a per-INSTALLATION key generated at first use and stored beside the licence — never Correlix's licence signing key, which does not exist on a customer host. The public key travels in the document, so `correlix-licence usage-verify <file>` checks it offline with nothing else. Same scoping as the usage read; a tenant's report carries no customer name and no licence id. Audited on both outcomes |

## Protocols

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/bgp/bmp/sessions` | BMP sessions the caller's routers have opened to the platform: router identity, up/closed state, per-peer BGP state (up \| down \| unknown — never an assumed up), message counts, dropped-update and parse-error counters |
| `GET` | `/api/bgp/bmp/stats` | The caller's own BMP aggregate — sessions, peers, messages by type, updates held/dropped, parse errors — plus the receiver's hard bounds, so a non-zero dropped count can be read against what it was measured against |
| `GET` | `/api/bgp/bmp/updates` | Recent per-prefix BGP updates from those sessions, newest first (?prefix= matches a prefix or anything inside it, ?peer=, ?session=, ?limit= 1..1000, ?cursor= opaque keyset). Announcements carry AS_PATH (AS4-merged), NEXT_HOP, ORIGIN, MED, LOCAL_PREF and communities incl. RFC 8092 large; a withdrawal carries none, because it has none |
| `GET` | `/api/protocols/&#123;proto&#125;/adjacencies` | Per-adjacency OSPF/IS-IS view for &#123;proto&#125; = ospf \| isis: live state where a series exists, plus the windowed change timeline from syslog/trap events, keyset-paged (?device=, ?since= 1m..7d, ?limit= 1..1000, ?cursor=). `up` is null for an event-only adjacency — history is not evidence of the state right now |
| `GET` | `/api/protocols/&#123;proto&#125;/health` | One device's IGP health for &#123;proto&#125; = ospf \| isis: neighbour/up/down counts (null without a live series), IS-IS levels, adjacency changes, flap count and a stability score that always carries the basis it was computed from. plus the depth blocks `lsdb` / `areas` / `spf_runs` / `timers`, each with its own coverage flag and each null + a note naming the absent series when nothing collects it — never 0 (?device= required, ?since= 1m..7d) |
| `GET` | `/api/protocols/&#123;proto&#125;/summary` | Fleet roll-up per device for &#123;proto&#125; = ospf \| isis, worst-first by flap count (?since= 1m..7d, ?limit= 1..500). `adjacencies` / `down_adjacencies` are LIVE counts and are null without a live series; a partial roll-up says so in `notes` and `truncated` |

| `GET` | `/api/security/exposure-stories` | Correlation objects grounded on security evidence |
| `GET` | `/api/security/exposure-stories/&#123;id&#125;` | One exposure story (delegates to the correlation detail) |
| `GET` | `/api/security/findings` | List security findings (cursor-paged; current=true collapses to the latest verdict per finding identity) |
| `GET` | `/api/security/findings/facets` | Facet counts by severity/status/seam/framework/evidence class |
| `GET` | `/api/security/findings/trend` | Verdict trend over time (date histogram by status) |
| `GET` | `/api/security/findings/&#123;id&#125;` | Fetch one finding (404 outside the caller's tenant) |
| `GET` | `/api/security/frameworks` | Compliance framework catalogue (id, name, version, base vs projection-of-800-53, scope) with the caller tenant's enable state, plus the published CIS device benchmarks and the section each hardening rule cites. `configured:false` means the tenant has not chosen and the shipped default set (NIST 800-53 Rev5 + CIS Controls) is shown |
| `PUT` | `/api/security/frameworks` | Choose which compliance frameworks the caller's tenant is assessed against (administration:write; body is [&#123;framework_id, enabled&#125;] over a closed vocabulary; the owner is stamped from the token and the cross-tenant view is refused) |
| `GET` | `/api/security/lane/status` | Security producer lane status: last scan id/time/outcome per tenant (own-only; cross-tenant for the platform admin) |
| `GET` | `/api/security/posture` | CTEM funnel, assessment coverage and last scan for the caller's tenant |
| `GET` | `/api/security/rules` | Detection catalog with the tenant's enable state (mitre is an ARRAY of ATT&CK technique ids, omitted when the rule carries none) |
| `PUT` | `/api/security/rules` | Enable/disable detections for the caller's tenant (administration:write) |
| `POST` | `/api/security/scan` | Queue a bounded security scan for the caller's own tenant (administration:write; 429 when one is already queued or running) |
| `GET` | `/api/security/views` | Saved findings filter sets for the caller's tenant |
| `POST` | `/api/security/views` | Save a findings filter set (infrastructure:write) |

## Telemetry

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/admin/parser/stats` | Parser rule corpus, per-rule hit counts, promotion rate and ingest pre-filter split, summed across the correlation replicas (platform admin) |
| `GET` | `/api/debug/loglevel` | Report each module's runtime log level and its armed auto-revert time — a LIVE reading for the switch this process owns, the last change requested through this api for the others, and the honest reason for a module that cannot be switched at runtime at all (platform admin) |
| `PUT` | `/api/debug/loglevel` | Raise one module to debug for a BOUNDED window (hard cap 30 minutes) with an auto-revert armed in the module's own process; a module with no runtime switch answers applied:false and says why, never a faked success (platform admin) |
| `GET` | `/api/debug/parsemarker` | Report whether the parser decision-trace filter is armed and when it auto-disarms (platform admin) |
| `PUT` | `/api/debug/parsemarker` | Arm the parser decision-trace filter on a needle for a BOUNDED window (hard cap 30 minutes) so a REAL, unmarked record's parse decisions are recorded; default-off and auto-disarming inside the traced process. An injected record carrying its own cx_debug marker is traced without this (platform admin) |
| `GET` | `/api/debug/sessions` | List the debug session directories this api has written, newest first: id, verb, kind, device, tenant, start time and the per-session verdict tally. An empty list always carries the reason it is empty (platform admin) |
| `GET` | `/api/debug/sessions/&#123;id&#125;` | One debug session: its manifest, timeline and human stage table, plus the module log files it holds (platform admin) |
| `GET` | `/api/debug/sessions/&#123;id&#125;/bundle` | Download a session as a redacted, checksummed tar.gz — SHA256SUMS inside the archive and the body's own digest in X-Correlix-Bundle-SHA256 (platform admin) |
| `GET` | `/api/debug/sessions/&#123;id&#125;/module/&#123;module&#125;` | One module's log file from a session, bounded in bytes and lines, with truncation stated rather than silent (platform admin) |
| `GET` | `/api/debug/stage/&#123;stage&#125;` | One stage's evidence for a marker (kafka\|opensearch\|victoria\|clickhouse\|correlation\|api, plus parser and ui on demand), with the exact query used (platform admin) |
| `POST` | `/api/debug/trace` | Inject ONE marked synthetic record (kind=syslog\|trap\|flow) into the stack's own ingress — never a device — and start the async follow; kind=gnmi is PASSIVE-ONLY (passive:true, device, since_seconds) and injects nothing, because a gNMI update originates on the device; returns the marker and a receipt (platform admin) |
| `GET` | `/api/debug/trace/&#123;marker&#125;` | Poll a trace's per-stage status: seen \| not_seen \| not_observable (with the reason) for the bus, the three stores, correlation and the api (platform admin) |
| `GET` | `/api/flows/top` | Top talkers (NetFlow/ClickHouse) |
| `POST` | `/api/logs/search` | Search logs (OpenSearch) |
| `GET` | `/api/metrics/query` | Instant PromQL query |
| `GET` | `/api/metrics/query_range` | Range PromQL query |
| `GET` | `/api/telemetry/unrecognized` | Mined templates of the caller's log lines the parser would not admit (days, limit, lane) |
| `POST` | `/api/telemetry/unrecognized/&#123;template_id&#125;/propose` | Draft a telemetry-catalog rule row and fixture for one unrecognized template — returned as text, applied nowhere (alerts:write) |
| `GET` | `/api/tunnels` | Overlay tunnel telemetry (IPsec/SD-WAN/GRE) |

## Troubleshooting

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/incidents/&#123;id&#125;/tac` | The escalation's state for one incident: classification, plan, collection job with per-command progress, stored bundles, case outcome, and the case connectors this tenant can actually use (infrastructure:read). An escalation started before an api restart is not resumed, and the response says so rather than showing an empty one |
| `GET` | `/api/incidents/&#123;id&#125;/tac/bundle` | Download the redacted evidence bundle as a zip: MANIFEST.json, the problem statement written under the evidence-only rule, per-command outputs, the incident's evidence timeline, topology, device facts and SHA256SUMS. ?profile=full\|email\|link_only picks how much it carries; the email profile trims the largest outputs first and names every omission in the manifest (infrastructure:read; audited as sensitive) |
| `POST` | `/api/incidents/&#123;id&#125;/tac/case` | Pre-fill the vendor/ITSM case form (submit:false) or perform the human-approved submission (submit:true). Case creation is never automatic. A connector without a create capability returns the paste-ready portal text and says so — a successful outcome, not a failure (infrastructure:write; audited) |
| `POST` | `/api/incidents/&#123;id&#125;/tac/case/refresh` | Re-read this incident's vendor case status now. It is floored at one refresh per case per 60 seconds so a person cannot be the thing that trips a vendor's rate limit; the automatic schedule is severity-tiered (Sev 1 every 2 minutes for 4 hours then every 5; Sev 2 every 5 for a day then every 15; Sev 3-4 every 15 then hourly) and degrades a whole tenant gracefully under a vendor's published limit, saying so on the chip. A failed read never renders as a stale status (infrastructure:read; audited) |
| `POST` | `/api/incidents/&#123;id&#125;/tac/classify` | Classify the incident into the closed issue-class taxonomy from evidence Correlix already holds — RCA hypotheses, alerts, matched protocol signatures, the selected Iris skill, log excerpts. Returns the class, the exact evidence that scored it, every alternative that scored, and the full class list so an operator can override to any class. Nothing matched is an ANSWER (the `generic` class, stated plainly), not an error (infrastructure:read; audited) |
| `POST` | `/api/incidents/&#123;id&#125;/tac/collect` | Start the read-only collection over the SSH gateway, or fold in operator-pasted outputs, or cancel a running one. `steps[]` carries the operator-REVIEWED command list (with an optional `template_id`, whose name/version the server looks up so provenance cannot be forged): every line is re-validated here against the output-only policy and the read-only grammar, and ONE refused line fails the WHOLE request naming it — a collection never silently drops a command and runs the rest. Asynchronous: returns the job, whose per-command progress is polled from GET …/tac. One collection per device at a time (409); 503 when no read-only transport is wired — never a fabricated capture (infrastructure:write; audited) |
| `POST` | `/api/incidents/&#123;id&#125;/tac/escalate` | ONE CLICK: classify the incident, build the command plan, choose the capture and the case connector, and start the read-only collection. It sends NOTHING — there is no path from this route to a vendor. The route is chosen by a documented ladder (your team's own route for this device's vendor, then the vendor's configured native path, then its mailbox, then portal text) and the response says which rung it used and why (infrastructure:write; audited) |
| `POST` | `/api/incidents/&#123;id&#125;/tac/escalate/confirm` | CLICK TWO: the human-approved submit, and the only route in this subtree that can cause a vendor case to exist. It re-applies the blockers to the form you actually submitted, so completing a field on the screen works and leaving it blank still refuses by name; then it opens the case, attaches the bundle where the connector can, and records the case id, URL and status on the incident (infrastructure:write, elevated identity; audited) |
| `POST` | `/api/incidents/&#123;id&#125;/tac/escalate/dry-run` | Prove this tenant's setup BEFORE the first real case: authenticate against the configured endpoint with the stored credential (a real, read-only call), then build the case payload a submit would send, run every validation the vendor's own schema and Correlix's required-field table impose, and show the exact request(s) — field by field, with the vendor's own field names where your onboarding bound them and every secret redacted. It creates, updates and attaches NOTHING. A pass proves the credential is accepted and the payload is complete; entitlement is still evaluated when the case is actually opened, and the report says so (infrastructure:write; audited) |
| `POST` | `/api/incidents/&#123;id&#125;/tac/escalate/prepare` | Build the redacted bundle and the pre-filled case form for the chosen route, and report whether the case could be opened. It sends NOTHING. The form arrives already carrying the serial and model from the device record and the contract and contact from your tenant's Ticket-delivery settings; anything the vendor demands and Correlix does not have is returned as a NAMED blocker with the vendor's own reason and the place it is set (infrastructure:write; audited) |
| `POST` | `/api/incidents/&#123;id&#125;/tac/plan` | Build the read-only command plan for a class on one of the caller's own devices: the vendor baseline set, the class deep-dive set, Correlix's own topology context, the size/time ceiling and the redaction note — shown BEFORE anything runs. Intents this dialect does not bind are listed as unbound; a platform with no authored plan runs nothing and says so rather than rendering another vendor's commands (infrastructure:read; audited) |
| `GET` | `/api/tac/captures` | This tenant's saved CAPTURES — a capture is a named list of commands — optionally narrowed to one CLI dialect with ?dialect=. A saved capture IS a command template: the same store, the same per-tenant isolation, and another tenant's capture is never listed (infrastructure:read) |
| `POST` | `/api/tac/captures` | Save a capture as one of this tenant's templates, so it is offered on the next escalation for that platform. The owner is stamped from the token — the body has no tenant field — and every command is validated server-side before the row exists (infrastructure:write; audited) |
| `POST` | `/api/tac/captures/upload` | Upload a command list and get a capture back. The file's bytes are the request body and ?filename= names it; the extension picks the parser — txt (one command per line, # comments), csv (command[,note]), json and yaml (&#123;"name","commands":[…]&#125;) or docx (every paragraph and table cell, read with archive/zip + encoding/xml). Bounded at 1 MiB, 500 commands and 512 characters per command. Every line is held to the SAME output-only policy the collector applies, and ONE refused line refuses the WHOLE file, reported by the line number in the uploaded file with the family and the rule that hit — nothing is silently dropped. It stores nothing: the capture becomes a row only when it is saved (infrastructure:write; audited) |
| `GET` | `/api/tac/captures/&#123;id&#125;` | One saved capture. A cross-tenant or unknown id answers the same 404 (infrastructure:read) |
| `GET` | `/api/tac/connectors` | The TAC case connectors as the calling tenant sees them: what each vendor or ITSM path can do (open the case, attach the bundle, read the status back), its attachment ceiling, its standing vendor research, and whether this tenant has brought credentials for it. `configured` is the only per-tenant field; a tenant that has stored nothing reads as not configured, which is a state and not an error (infrastructure:read) |
| `DELETE` | `/api/tac/connectors/&#123;id&#125;` | Remove this tenant's settings for one case connector. Other connectors' settings are untouched, and escalations stop offering this path (infrastructure:write; audited on both outcomes) |
| `GET` | `/api/tac/connectors/&#123;id&#125;` | One case connector's stored settings for the calling tenant, with every write-only secret REMOVED: `secrets` reports only which of them are stored. `config_section` names the settings block this connector edits (servicenow, jira, email, cisco, juniper) and is empty for the portal-only paths, which hold no credential at all. The email block's `auth_mode` selects which of its fields matter — password (an SMTP relay), microsoft365 (Graph sendMail), google_workspace (the Gmail API) or smtp_oauth (SASL XOAUTH2); a blank one is the relay (infrastructure:read) |
| `PUT` | `/api/tac/connectors/&#123;id&#125;` | Bring or change this tenant's credentials for one case connector. The owner is stamped from the token — the body has no tenant field, and an unknown field is refused — and the body carries only that connector's own fields. A secret that is absent keeps the stored one, an empty string CLEARS it, a value replaces it; the connector's own validator refuses an incomplete configuration by naming the field (infrastructure:write; audited on both outcomes) |
| `POST` | `/api/tac/connectors/&#123;id&#125;/test` | Ask the vendor one READ-ONLY question with the stored credentials — Jira /myself, a ServiceNow table read, Juniper's own list of legal priorities, and for a mail path whichever question its mailbox sign-in implies: SMTP connect + EHLO + STARTTLS + AUTH on a relay, a Microsoft Graph /users/&#123;mailbox&#125; read on a Microsoft 365 mailbox, a Gmail users.getProfile read on a Google Workspace one. It creates, updates and attaches nothing. Bounded by a timeout, and the answer is a named outcome (ok, not_configured, refused, unreachable, timed_out, unsupported) with the vendor's own words; a path that publishes no read-only check says so (infrastructure:write; audited) |
| `GET` | `/api/tac/learning` | This tenant's TAC learning backlog: for each collection, the commands whose output no parser recognised — with the reason (no parser authored for the concept, none for this platform, or a parser that ran and could not read it), a bounded REDACTED excerpt and the full output size — plus this tenant's signature candidates and the per-kind gap tally. ?dialect= narrows it. Per-tenant data: a cross-tenant principal must scope into a tenant first (infrastructure:read) |
| `POST` | `/api/tac/learning/candidates` | Write a TAC answer down as a signature CANDIDATE. The owner is stamped from the token — the body has no tenant field — free text is redacted and bounded, a citation must be an https link, and every command passes the SAME output-only policy and read-only grammar the collector applies at the wire; `proposed_class` is derived from the taxonomy, not claimed. A candidate is a proposal: nothing here is matched against anything or shown as coverage (infrastructure:write; audited) |
| `DELETE` | `/api/tac/learning/candidates/&#123;id&#125;` | Drop one of this tenant's signature candidates (infrastructure:write; audited) |
| `GET` | `/api/tac/learning/candidates/&#123;id&#125;` | One signature candidate. A cross-tenant or unknown id answers the same 404 (infrastructure:read) |
| `PUT` | `/api/tac/learning/candidates/&#123;id&#125;` | Revise a candidate. Identity and provenance are immutable across the edit (id, owner, author, creation time); the whole proposal is re-validated and one refused command fails the whole request, naming the line (infrastructure:write; audited) |
| `GET` | `/api/tac/learning/export` | This tenant's candidates for one dialect (?dialect=, required) rendered as the research YAML scripts/tac-merge-research.py consumes — an attachment a human reviews and merges. It changes nothing: the shipped catalogue, the V1 replay pin and the doc_claimed verification gate are untouched by an export (infrastructure:read; audited) |
| `DELETE` | `/api/tac/routing` | Remove this tenant's TAC routing record. Escalations still work; they simply arrive with nothing pre-filled (infrastructure:write; audited) |
| `GET` | `/api/tac/routing` | This tenant's TAC routing: the named human a vendor calls back, which connector carries which vendor's cases, the preferred capture per CLI dialect, and the support contracts a case is entitled with (per vendor, and per device serial where a vendor entitles per chassis). Per-tenant data: a cross-tenant principal must scope into a tenant first (infrastructure:read) |
| `PUT` | `/api/tac/routing` | Save this tenant's TAC routing. The owner is stamped from the token — the body has no tenant field and an unknown field is refused — every free-text field is bounded, a route naming a connector this platform does not have is refused, and a record that ends up holding nothing is REMOVED so a tenant that cleared its last setting reads exactly like one that never made any (infrastructure:write; audited) |
| `GET` | `/api/tac/templates` | This tenant's saved TAC command templates plus Correlix's read-only defaults, optionally narrowed to one CLI dialect with ?dialect=. Per-tenant data: a cross-tenant principal must scope into a tenant first, and another tenant's template is never listed (infrastructure:read) |
| `POST` | `/api/tac/templates` | Save a command set for one dialect. The owner is stamped from the token — the body has no tenant field — and every command is validated server-side before the row exists: config/restart/daemon commands are refused BY NAME with the family and the rule that hit, a ping/traceroute must be inside the bounded-probe limits, and everything else must pass the read-only grammar. A refusal returns per-line verdicts, never a bare "invalid" (infrastructure:write; audited) |
| `GET` | `/api/tac/templates/defaults` | Correlix's own command templates, generated deterministically from the authored per-dialect plans: one baseline set per dialect plus one per issue class that dialect binds commands for. Reference data, identical for every tenant, immutable. ?dialect= narrows it; a platform with no authored plan honestly returns none rather than another vendor's commands (infrastructure:read) |
| `POST` | `/api/tac/templates/validate` | Per-line verdicts for a command list on one dialect — what the review step calls as the operator types. Each line reports ok/refused, the forbidden family and rule when the output-only policy refused it, and the origin of an accepted line: `catalog` (a rendering of an authored Correlix command) or `custom` (written by your team, output-only and read-only, never verified by Correlix on this platform). It reads nothing and stores nothing; the authoritative check still runs on the way into a template and on the way into a collection (infrastructure:read) |
| `DELETE` | `/api/tac/templates/&#123;id&#125;` | Remove one of this tenant's templates. Correlix defaults cannot be deleted — they are generated from the authored plans, not stored rows (infrastructure:write; audited) |
| `GET` | `/api/tac/templates/&#123;id&#125;` | One template, with `diff_vs_default` when it was forked from a Correlix default and that default still ships. A cross-tenant or unknown id answers the same 404 (infrastructure:read) |
| `PUT` | `/api/tac/templates/&#123;id&#125;` | Replace a template's commands, name or description. Identity is immutable (id, owner, author, creation time, source) and the version increments, so a bundle can name the exact revision that ran. A Correlix default is read-only — 403 with the reason, and the operator saves a copy instead. Another tenant's id is a 404 (infrastructure:write; audited) |
| `POST` | `/api/troubleshoot/protocol-diagnostics/analyze` | Run the failure signatures over supplied `show` output; returns the verdict + cause + remediation, or an honest "no known signature matched" (infrastructure:read). `analyzed:false` with `not_analyzed` set is the DISTINCT state for a request that carried no output at all — nothing was scored, so the protocol's state is unknown rather than clean |
| `GET` | `/api/troubleshoot/protocol-diagnostics/catalog` | The 15-issue BGP/OSPF/IS-IS matrix: symptoms, dialect coverage and the per-issue read-only command bundle. The rendered CLI dialect is chosen by ?vendor=&lt;platform string&gt; OR by ?device=&lt;id&gt; resolved in the caller's own inventory (cross-tenant/unknown id → 404); supplying both, or any other query parameter, is a 400 — a selector that changes which commands an operator is shown is never silently ignored |
| `POST` | `/api/troubleshoot/protocol-diagnostics/collect` | Run an issue's read-only command bundle against one of the caller's own devices; output is secret-redacted (infrastructure:write; 503 when no command source is wired) |
| `POST` | `/api/troubleshoot/protocol-diagnostics/export` | Assemble the redacted "Send to TAC" bundle from supplied outputs, optionally with the signature analysis folded in (infrastructure:read; audited) |
| `GET` | `/api/troubleshoot/tac/knowledge` | Iris's TAC coverage: the issue-class taxonomy, the intent vocabulary, and per vendor dialect which intents are bound, which commands are verified against a real capture versus taken from vendor documentation, and which recognised platforms have NO authored plan at all. Version-pinned reference data, identical for every tenant (infrastructure:read) |
